newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: E.Asia Oilseeds - S.Korea buying, others sidelined.
newsitem.headline: E.Asia Oilseeds - S.Korea buying, others sidelined.

text.p: South Korean feedmillers are seen buying over 70,000 tonnes of meal over the next few weeks while the rest of the East Asian oilseeds trade is staying on the sidelines waiting for prices to ease, dealers said on Monday.
They said several groups in South Korea are expected to seek 7,000 tonnes of rapeseed meal and 13,000 tonnes of cottonseed meal this week, both for July onwards arrival.

Korea's National Livestock Cooperatives Federation (NLCF) said it will invite tenders for 14,000 tonnes of rapeseed meal, 6,500 tonnes of cottonseed meal, 8,000 tonnes of grain screening pellet and 25,000 tonnes of palm kernel meal on Tuesday.
South Korean soybean crushers expressed a preference for Brazilian soybeans for April/June shipments in place of high-priced U.S. origins, they said.
Soybean buyers in Japan, Taiwan and the Philippines are seen staying out of the market as they currently have ample domestic supplies and are waiting for high Chicago prices to ease.

The May soybean contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) finished on Friday 5-1/2 U.S. cents up on the day at US$8.44 a bushel. The May contract was indicated up two U.S. cents at $8.46 a bushel on the exchange's after hours Project A trading system at 0640 GMT on Monday.
The Japanese have also bought South American beans for their nearby requirements, dealers said.
"We'd like to watch the price direction before we resume buying," a soybean trader at a major trade house in Tokyo said.
"We've already covered our nearby requirements. I'd like to see whether the market rises further from current levels before returning to the market," another trader said.

In Taiwan, the Kaohsiung division of the Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association backed out of a plan to tender for 54,000 tonnes of soybeans for June delivery due to excess soymeal inventories being held by buyers, dealers said.
Buyers in the Philippines plan to stay out of the market after putting on ample coverage through June, dealers said.
